<thought>The proton NMR spectra indicate the presence of aromatic protons (7.04 ppm) and various aliphatic protons, including methyl groups (1.12 ppm, 2.21 ppm, 2.34 ppm) and methine/methylene groups (2.04 ppm, 2.70 ppm, 4.01 ppm). The presence of aromatic protons and the chemical shifts suggest a possible aromatic ring with substituents. To further refine the structure, I will use the IR spectra to identify any functional groups, such as carbonyls, which are not easily identified by NMR alone.</thought>
<action>ir_spectra</action>

<thought>The IR spectra show peaks at 3357 cm⁻¹, which could indicate the presence of an -OH or -NH group, and peaks around 1606 and 1587 cm⁻¹, which are typical for aromatic C=C stretching. The absence of a strong peak around 1700 cm⁻¹ suggests there is no carbonyl group present. Given the data from the NMR and IR spectra, the compound likely contains an aromatic ring with alkyl substituents and possibly an alcohol or amine group. To further refine the structure, I will search for similar compounds in the NMRShift database using the information gathered so far.</thought>
<action>search_by_smiles</action>
<action_input>{"smiles": "C1=CC=CC=C1", "top_k": 5}</action_input>

<thought>The search results from the NMRShift database show compounds with similar aromatic structures, but none match the exact chemical shifts observed in the 13C and 1H NMR spectra. The presence of both aromatic and aliphatic components, along with the IR spectra indicating a possible -OH or -NH group, suggests a more complex structure. To further refine the structure, I will use the HSQC NMR spectra to correlate the carbon and hydrogen environments, which can help identify specific functional groups and connectivity.</thought>

<thought>The HSQC NMR spectra provide correlations between hydrogen and carbon environments, confirming the presence of aromatic protons (7.04-7.06 ppm) with corresponding carbons (128.7, 128.4, 130.4, 124.9 ppm) and aliphatic protons with their respective carbons.
